description: Machine-readable negative cursor vectors mirrored from zh/conformance/conformance-vectors.md section 1.16. Complements the positive opaqueness vector ak.vector.encoding.cursor_opaque.core.v1: every case below is a schema-valid-looking ak:cursor: token that a conformant receiver MUST reject before advancing any server-side state. reason_code values are stable codes from error-code-registry.json (invalid_cursor is surfaced under top-level invalid_param).

cases.name: oversized_token
cases.violation: encoded token exceeds the 4KB body cap before any decode work

cases.name: invalid_base64url
cases.violation: token payload is not unpadded base64url

cases.name: malformed_json
cases.violation: decoded body is not valid JSON

cases.name: duplicate_json_key
cases.violation: duplicate JSON key violates canonical JSON ingress rules

cases.name: non_nfc_string
cases.violation: decoded t string value is not Unicode NFC (it carries U+0065 U+0301 instead of the NFC composed form U+00E9); canonical JSON ingress MUST reject. The raw body is intentionally not inlined here so this fixture file itself stays NFC-clean; the base64url token is the authoritative input.

cases.name: inline_positions_rejected
cases.violation: v1 core cursor body carries only the opaque handle; inline position state (s) violates the closed {v,purpose,t,x,h} schema

cases.name: unsupported_version
cases.violation: cursor version is not in supported_versions (v1 core supports only "1")

cases.name: handle_too_short
cases.violation: stateful handle h is shorter than the 22-character minimum (>=128 bits of entropy)

cases.name: non_canonical_timestamp
cases.violation: t must be a canonical UTC Z timestamp; the +00:00 offset form is rejected

cases.name: stream_ttl_exceeds_cap
cases.violation: x - t exceeds the stream-purpose hard TTL cap of 7 days (encoding.md section 8.3 rule 12)

cases.name: barrier_ttl_exceeds_cap
cases.violation: x - t exceeds the barrier-purpose hard TTL cap of 1 hour (encoding.md section 8.3 rule 12)

cases.name: expired
cases.violation: x expiry is in the past

vectors.fixture_freshness_note: All timestamps are pinned so every case stays deterministically rejectable for the spec lifetime: expired cases use year-2020 values (always past), TTL-cap and negative-TTL cases use year-2099 x values (not expired before 2099) with a violation that is checked before any now-relative comparison could differ.
rules: receivers MUST reject every case before advancing subscription position, barrier wait, or any other server-side state

syntax / schema / TTL-bound failures surface as top-level invalid_param with reason_code invalid_cursor; expiry uses cursor_expired; handle lookup or cross-binding failures (not covered here, they need server state) use cursor_integrity_invalid
receivers MUST enforce the 4KB cap on the encoded token before spending base64 or JSON parsing work
TTL bound checks MUST validate t well-formedness first, then t <= x, then t not in the future beyond clock skew, then x - t against the per-purpose cap, so a corrupt t cannot bypass the cap
